name: keendreams
title: Keen Dreams (id Software / Softdisk, Borland C++ / DOS)
_doc: THE FIRST 16-BIT TARGET, and it is not expected to build yet. PRISM emits for i386 and only for i386; this program is Borland C++ real mode, with 242 `far` declarations and 141 uses of MK_FP/FP_SEG/FP_OFF/_seg/int86 across its C. It is here to be a MEASUREMENT: a build that fails loudly names what a 16-bit backend has to supply, which is cheaper and truer than estimating it. gate-abi16 and gate-bits16 already pin the layout rules against Open Watcom for exactly this day.
_why_this_one: Chosen over Wolf3D, Catacomb 3D and Hovertank 3D, and the first version of this note chose it on HALF the evidence: it counted .ASM files and missed the inline assembly inside the C, which the second build then stopped on. Re-measured with both halves -- .ASM lines / C-visible entry points / inline asm statements / segment-register touches: KeenDreams 3,802 / 25 / 640 / 95; Wolf3D 1,951 / 18 / 1,127 / 247; Catacomb3D 4,159 / 37 / 1,288 / 276; Hovertank3D 14,685 / 202 / 373 / 64. On raw assembly VOLUME Wolf3D is now the smaller. What still puts Keen Dreams first is the NATURE of it: the fewest segment-register touches of the three whose files are tractable, and .ASM entry points that are ordinary routines (VW_Plot, VW_DrawTile8, RFL_UpdateTiles...) where Wolf3D's include three timer interrupt handlers and self-modifying 386 detection. The resemblance to Jump 'n Bump's get_block/put_block holds for those files ONLY: inline assembly is interleaved with C inside function bodies and cannot be bound as a separate function. That is the hard part, for all four.
_units: The program's own list, read out of kdreams.prj -- a binary Borland project whose file names sit in it as plain text. Worth the trouble: the tree also carries lscr/loadscn2.c and static/makeobj.c, and the project names neither. BUT the .prj records DEPENDENCIES as well as project items, and reading every name out of it took one too many: id_us_s.c is #included by id_us.c:516, so it is part of that unit and not one of its own. Compiled alone it failed at its line 19 for want of the context id_us.c gives it, which is how the mistake showed. 17 units.
_asm: FOUR assembly objects the project builds and this target does not: id_vw_a.asm, id_vw_ae.asm, id_rf_a.asm, id_us_a.asm. They are MASM/TASM, and PRISM's assembler front end reads NASM (src/asm/nasm.js), so there is nothing to bind them with yet -- the build will report their symbols as undefined, which IS the survey. id_vw_ac.asm is in the tree and NOT in the project: it is the CGA variant, and GRMODE in id_heads.h ships as EGAGR. Selecting neither: EGA is what the tree already says.
_static_data: make.bat runs static/makeobj.c over the .KDR files in static/ to produce KDREDICT.OBJ and KDREHEAD.OBJ, which the project LINKS. PRISM links no object files, so that data has no route in today. Named here rather than discovered later.
_first_gap: MEASURED TWICE. First stop: ID_MM.H:43, `typedef void _seg * memptr;` -- Borland's segment pointer, a pointer kind rather than a qualifier. The parser now accepts _seg and huge immediately before a star and marks the pointer; any function that reaches one is refused by name, and any sizeof/offsetof/_Alignof of a type holding one is refused rather than folded (types.js segPtr explains why the placeholder size cannot be left undefined). Second stop: kd_play.c:592, `asm mov es,[WORD PTR mapsegs+4]` -- Borland's statement form of inline assembly. 640 such statements in 11 of this program's 20 C files, 95 of them touching a segment register directly. kd_main.c and kd_demo.c parse whole.
_caseInsensitive: id_us.c includes "ID_US_S.c" and the file is id_us_s.c. It resolved here only because this machine's filesystem ignores case; on Linux it would not. DOS never had to care.
_survey: SURVEYED UNIT BY UNIT, because one build stops at the first failure and the survey is the point. 16 of 17 units parse, and the one that does not is a DECISION rather than a gap: id_ca.c:1471, `#if BUFFERSIZE < sizeof(maptype)`, refused by name and staying refused -- sizeof in a preprocessor condition is Borland's, not C's, every conforming compiler rejects that file, and the #if sits inside a function body so there is not even a valid partial unit to read types from. It guards a compile-time assertion whose body is an English sentence, the idiom that predates #error, and it is the only occurrence in the corpus. Cleared, each with its own gate: NULL in kd_keen.c and kd_act1.c, from <STDIO.H> and friends written in capitals (gate-include-case); `static void interrupt` in id_in.c and id_sd.c (gate-borland16); a lone 0x1A in the file id_us.c includes, the DOS end-of-file marker, this being the only built target whose sources carry one (gate-dos-eof); `boolean inline = false;` in kd_act2.c, a C99 keyword five years early (gate-c89-inline); and kd_play.c's locationless `#`, which was a `#pragma warn -pro` sitting between an `else` and the statement it governs -- legal C anywhere, and the one of three pragma positions the parser did not step over (gate-pragma-position). Truly absent, and still reported: alloc.h, mem.h, process.h. THE PARSER IS NO LONGER THE SUBJECT. What the 16 that parse are refused FOR, under dos16m and after `_seg` pointers (gate-segptr) took the count from 144 functions to 81: Borland inline assembly (32), `huge` (5), and the DOS interrupt-vector surface -- the pseudo-registers _AX/_AH/_AL/_ES/_CX with getvect/setvect/poke/harderr. Those three, and a 16-bit backend to put under them.
_compile: No compiler identity macro is tested anywhere in the source and no #pragma pack or option appears, so the memory model is entirely a Borland project setting rather than anything the C states. That is itself a finding: nothing in the source tells a reader which model it wants.
_c89: Borland C++ 2.0 predates C99, and kd_act2.c:1404 uses the word: `boolean inline = false;`, then assigns to it and tests it. The flag gives `inline` back as an identifier and nothing else -- the GNU spellings __inline and __inline__ stay keywords, and no program here uses restrict or _Bool as a name.
_model: dos16m, the MEDIUM model -- the one the program declares in its own assembly: `MODEL MEDIUM,C` in id_rf_a.asm and id_us_a.asm, which must match the C it links with. Far code, four-byte function pointers; near data, two-byte data pointers; `far` and `near` honoured wherever they are written (gate-abi16m, against Watcom -mm). DGROUP sits at linear 0 so a near pointer and its linear address are the same number; the near statics end at 0xBE41 and the seven far objects that are defined -- son, prnt, freq, text_buf, d_code, d_len, mmblocks -- live from 0x10000 (gate-farobj). Of the twelve the source declares far, story, gametext and maphead are externs defined in the static-data .OBJ files PRISM does not link, and p_len and p_code sit inside `#if INCLUDE_LZH_COMP`, which is 0. HISTORY: this target was briefly dos16l, on a deduction from the size of its statics that had been measured in i386 type sizes; it is retracted in the commit that found MODEL MEDIUM. run() refuses any model but i386, so nothing executes yet.
_signedChar: NOT DECLARED, and that is a measurement rather than an omission. Borland's default char is signed, but whether this build had -K set is in the same binary .PRJ the memory model could not be read from -- so the question was put to the code instead. Compiling the program twice, signedChar true and false, and comparing each function's output leaves 9 of 404 emitted functions that read a plain char. None depends on its sign for any value the program produces: the keyboard path fills LastASCII from ASCIINames/ShiftNames/SpecialNames, declared `byte` with no entry above 127; US_Print and US_CPrint compare the char only with 0 and '\n'; USL_ScreenDraw writes the character byte and the attribute byte separately, so the CP437 box characters 0xDC-0xDF in id_us_s.c land as the same byte either way. US_CheckParm hands a command-line char to isalpha, which is undefined for a negative value -- a latent bug of the original under Borland, reachable only by typing a byte above 0x7F. NOT COVERED: the 145 functions refused today (segmented pointers, inline assembly) compile to stubs, so this diff cannot see into them; it is to be rerun once they emit.
